After 15 years at the helm, today officially marks Tim Cook's final day as Apple's CEO. In April this year, Apple announced that Cook would step down as CEO on September 1, with John Ternus taking over.

Of course, Cook won't be completely leaving. He will transition to the role of Executive Chairman of Apple's Board of Directors.

Tim Cook's final day as Apple CEO

Cook became Apple's CEO in 2011, just two months after the death of Steve Jobs. Ternus, meanwhile, joined Apple's product design team in 2001, rose rapidly through the ranks, and was officially promoted to Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering in January 2021.

A Bloomberg report over the weekend reiterated that, in his role as Executive Chairman, Cook will focus on managing Apple's relationships with President Trump and the Chinese government.

Bloomberg noted that Ternus is expected to use Cook's current office after taking over. According to The Information, Cook's executive assistant will remain in place and transition to working for Ternus.

Apple reportedly held a farewell dinner for Cook at Apple Park last week, featuring "hours-long speeches from Ternus, Laurene Powell Jobs, and other current and former Apple executives." Cook's favourite band OneRepublic also performed at the event.

The handover comes ahead of Apple's "Surprise and Shine" special event, scheduled for Wednesday, September 9. Cook will not appear at the event, which will be led by Ternus. Apple is expected to unveil a foldable iPhone Ultra, the iPhone 18 Pro, new Apple Watch models, and more.

In recent weeks, Apple has announced a series of unpopular decisions, including price hikes on most hardware products (excluding iPhones) as well as subscription services like Apple TV, Apple Music, and Apple One. This sets the stage for Ternus to focus on what has been described as the most ambitious product cycle in Apple's history.

Are you looking forward to Ternus taking over as Apple CEO tomorrow? What changes would you like to see him make? How would you rate Cook's tenure? Let us know in the comments.
